So a little background first: I love ASOIAF and I recently became a full fledged book hipster in that I am boycotting the show due to the shifting nature of the plot. It is not the book series anymore than let's say, Alexander (the movie), accurately reflects the life of Alexander the Great. I understand that the books are not the show, and I am not here to bitch about that, I just want to explain that D&D in their relentless pursuit of rating have destroyed what I used to love.

Anyway, on to the hypothesis:

I think Euron raped, or at least, sexually molested his younger brother Aeron when they were children. This is nothing new to those of us whom have read and analyzed the series, but it is something that interests me as I believe the Ironborn to be more than the baseless half wit pirates that many other book readers believe them to be. I am also very interested in sexuality, identity and agency in the series, and if Aeron was molested by his brother, that event would have most certainly shaped his identity and agency as an actor in the book series.

So let's look at the evidence:

There is certainly not an abundance of evidence for my particular hypothesis; aside from the fact that Aeron has a great disdain for Euron which is overwhelmingly present, there are only a few sentences which really lend any sort of weight to the case that I am trying to make.

Passage 1

That man is dead. Aeron had drowned and been reborn from the sea, the god’s own prophet. No mortal man could frighten him, no more than the darkness could…nor memories, the bones of the soul. The sound of a door opening, the scream of a rusted hinge. Euron has come again**. It did not matter. He was the Damphair priest, beloved of the god.

That man is dead

That man being the man that Aeron formerly was. A weak man, a man with fear in his heart, a man that maybe, was not truly a man, as in Ironborn culture being raped by another man, and the very act of penetration, would most likely be seen as a very weak and feminine thing.

Aeron had drowned and been reborn from the sea, the god’s own prophet.

Aeron, as we know, is a Priest of the Drowned God, and in an ultimate sacrifice to their god, the Ironborn literally drown themselves and then are revived by the Priests, who seem to know CPR. This act of drowning is very symbolic, not only in Ironborn culture, but for Aeron personally. He views himself as a new man now that he has died and been reborn, from the sea no less (the home of their god), and in this act he has become an entirely new person in his own mind, and as we have seen from the deference other pay to him, in the minds of many of his fellow Ironborn (whether that deference be out of fear or respect matters not, they still see him as a new man).

No mortal man could frighten him, no more than the darkness could…nor memories, the bones of the soul.

Now that Aeron is a new man he is no longer frightened by any mortal men, he had died after all, what need of fear is there after one has already died? Not only had he died, but he had arisen reborn from the sea as a prophet of his god. Just as fearing the darkness is a childish thing, and as an adult childhood is most certainly a past and alien life, so too is the fear of man something alien that existed only within his past life. His memories, the memories of another life, are also something which we can see he no longer fears. He no longer fears such memories as they are those of another man, a dead man, who drowned and never walked out of the sea.

The sound of a door opening, the scream of a rusted hinge.** Euron has come again**.

Here is the rape. The sound of the door opening, the scream of a rusted hinge. Why would a rusted hinge scream, and not say, creak or groan, as they are usually described as doing in literature. I do not think this was an accident of language, I think Martin is being very precise in his word usage here: the hinge screamed because Aeron could not. And immediately after that sentence we are told that Euron has come, again. The scream of the hinge, or as I think, the silent scream of Aeron signifies the approach of his rapist, again. That again part is particularly haunting, Aeron had most likely been raped or molested several times by his brother.

Before we go on to analyze the final sentence I would like to talk more about the silent scream of young Aeron by analyzing Ironborn culture a bit. This is a culture that revels in the suffering of others. The house words of the Greyjoys are "We Do Not Sow", meaning very plainly that they take what they want, often by force. The Ironborn seem to delight in raiding others and carrying off their gold and women. The rape of a woman by a man is likely of no concern, unless it was an Ironborn man raping an Ironborn woman, as we can make a case that the Ironborn believe woman to be the property of a man; this we can see in the salt wives that many Ironborn men take as trophies of their raids along with other booty.

So what would happen if a man raped another man? I don't think anything would happen to the rapist. I don't think the rapist would be seen as being wrong, or homosexual, I think others may think the rapist to be aberrant of the norm, maybe people would speak of him behind his back, but I believe no action would be taken against him. Why do I believe that? Because psychologically, rape is not about sex, it is about dominance, it is about control, it is about degradation. Rape denies a person of agency, in that they are deprived the ability to have ultimate control over there own body. Rape is also about power, in denying the person being raped self sovereignty the rapist is in complete control of that person. So raping a man would probably be no sweat of an Ironborn man's back (or dick, for that matter). It isn't homosexual to them, it is about establishing dominance and proving themselves the strongest.

But as for the person, or in this case man, or more accurately boy, that was raped, what of them? I believe that any man or boy that was raped would be seen as a woman, in that they were penetrated by a man and did not have the strength or force of will to stop it. They would be seen as less than, since they were denied all self sovereignty and agency. This is why I think Aeron could not, or did not scream; he knew of the consequences to be suffered, not for his brother, but for himself. He already thought of himself as weak and girlish as he thinks "Nine sons were born from the loins of Quellon Greyjoy, and I was the least of them, as weak and frightened as a girl", so what would his great father have said to know that he was penetrated like a woman, what would the other Ironborn say knowing he had been raped? Aeron would have never lived that down at the very least, and at the very worst, he may have been cast from his House. So the rusted hinge screamed for him when he could not.

It did not matter. He was the Damphair priest, beloved of the god.

But as we see, none of these things matter now to Aeron, for he is the Damphair, prophet and beloved of the Ironborn god. But I think these things really do matter, as I don't think Aeron ever truly got over this. I mean, how could anyone ever get over being raped?

Passage 2 (really just two sentences)

No mortal man could frighten him, no more than the darkness could, or the bones of his soul, the grey and grisly bones of his soul. The sound of a door opening, the scream of a rusted iron hinge.

This passage comes after Aeron meets Euron again for the first time in many years, and Aeron flees from his brother "as if he were still the weak thing he had been". After his encounter with Euron these are the thoughts that come to Aeron's mind:

No mortal man could frighten him, no more than the darkness could, or the bones of his soul, the grey and grisly bones of his soul.

Here we have Aeron once again reminding himself that no mortal man could frighten him, but reminding may not be the proper phrase, lying to himself, may be better. If mortal men could not truly frighten him why would he think this over and over; I believe he must continually remind himself mortal men do not frighten him lest he forget, and once again become that "weak and girlsih" thing he used to be. And again we have a reference to his past memories, those "grey and grisly bones of his soul", which it seems, despite the death and rebirth, he cannot let go of. Aeron Damphair, it seems, is a lie, a cloak used to to hide the visage of a lost and cowering little boy. Poor Aeron....

The sound of a door opening, the scream of a rusted iron hinge.

Potent and imagery, and downright fucking creepy. A screaming hinge that was speaking for Aeron when he could not, foretelling the abuse that was to come.

So that is our paltry evidence for Aeron being raped, or molested, on several occasions by his elder brother Euron Crow's Eye. And I use his current moniker, Aeron, as I believe these memories are holding him back and did not truly allow him to become a new man reborn from the sea; that is, the Damphair.

Let me know what you guys think about this, albeit old, hypothesis. It is one that doesn't get brought up on the forums a lot and I wanted to know how others felt about it. And excuse me if I have run a bit here and there. It has been a long time since I typed up a theory like this.

Thanks for your time,
